name: EN 206:2013+A2:2021 — generic European recommended values
jurisdiction: EU (generic; national annexes override these values)

source.table: Table F.1 (informative Annex F — recommended limiting values for composition and properties of concrete)
source.verification_note: Indicative values for design exploration, reconstructed from secondary-source summaries of Table F.1, NOT transcribed from a purchased copy of the standard. National annexes vary (see bs8500.json for one). Check against the published standard before any structural or tender use.

XC1.description: Corrosion induced by carbonation — dry or permanently wet
XC1.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XC2.description: Corrosion induced by carbonation — wet, rarely dry
XC2.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XC3.description: Corrosion induced by carbonation — moderate humidity
XC3.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XC4.description: Corrosion induced by carbonation — cyclic wet and dry
XC4.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XD1.description: Corrosion induced by chlorides other than seawater — moderate humidity
XD1.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XD2.description: Corrosion induced by chlorides other than seawater — wet, rarely dry
XD2.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XD3.description: Corrosion induced by chlorides other than seawater — cyclic wet and dry
XD3.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XS1.description: Corrosion induced by chlorides from seawater — airborne salt, no direct contact
XS1.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XS2.description: Corrosion induced by chlorides from seawater — permanently submerged
XS2.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XS3.description: Corrosion induced by chlorides from seawater — tidal, splash and spray zones
XS3.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XF1.description: Freeze/thaw attack — moderate water saturation, no de-icing agent
XF1.notes: min_air_pct intentionally omitted (not null): air entrainment provisions for XF classes exist in Table F.1 but the numeric minimum depends on nominal max aggregate size, which is not confidently recalled here. The engine reports UNKNOWN for this rule rather than a guessed threshold.

XF2.description: Freeze/thaw attack — moderate water saturation, with de-icing agent
XF2.notes: min_air_pct intentionally omitted (not null); see XF1 note.

XF3.description: Freeze/thaw attack — high water saturation, no de-icing agent
XF3.notes: min_air_pct intentionally omitted (not null); see XF1 note.

XF4.description: Freeze/thaw attack — high water saturation, with de-icing agent or seawater
XF4.notes: min_air_pct intentionally omitted (not null); see XF1 note.

XA1.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

XA2.notes: min_strength_MPa intentionally omitted: secondary sources for Table F.1 disagree between C25/30 and C30/37 for XA2, so this is left UNKNOWN rather than guessed.

XA3.notes: w/b uses total binder; k-value substitution not modelled here.

notes: This pack is unverified secondary-source recall of EN 206 Table F.1, not a transcription of the purchased standard (see source.verification_note). Two categories of rule are deliberately omitted, not guessed: (1) max_scm_fraction is omitted for every class — SCM replacement limits are governed by EN 206 Sec 5.2.5 k-value provisions and EN 197-1 cement-type designations, which this pack does not model (see spec's Accepted exclusions); a class without this key means UNKNOWN, not 'unconstrained'. (2) min_air_pct is omitted (not null) for XF1-XF4 because the standard's air-entrainment minimum is aggregate-size dependent and was not confidently recalled; min_strength_MPa is similarly omitted for XA2 due to conflicting secondary-source recall. Every other numeric value above should still be checked against the published table before any real design use.
